mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances following a sustained increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a sharp increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period signals supply-side constraints, which can lead to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances following a decrease in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over a 3-month period, coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances following the combined increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period indicates deflationary pressures, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances following a sustained decrease in CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a sharp increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over a quarter signals economic contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE).
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances following a decrease in GDPC1, especially when accompanied by a rise in UNRATE.
